skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A taxi charges a \$3 fee plus \$2 for each kilometer traveled. A rider has at most \$25 to spend. What is the greatest whole number of kilometers the rider can travel?
questions.explanation: $3 + 2k \le 25$ gives $k \le 11$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $x$ satisfies the inequality $3x - 4 > 11$?
questions.explanation: $3x > 15$, so $x > 5$. Only 6 is greater than 5.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which point $(x, y)$ is a solution to the system of inequalities $y > 2x - 3$ and $y < -x + 6$?
questions.explanation: For $(1, 2)$: $2 > -1$ and $2 < 5$, so both hold. Each other point fails at least one inequality.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A rowboat can safely carry at most 450 kilograms, including the person rowing it. The rower weighs 72 kilograms, and each sack of rice weighs 25 kilograms. Which inequality represents the possible numbers of sacks, $s$, that the boat can safely carry along with the rower?
questions.explanation: The total load is the rower plus the sacks, $72 + 25s$, and "at most" means $\le 450$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Emma is saving to buy a telescope that costs \$1,500. She has already saved \$420 and will save \$90 each week. What is the least number of weeks she must save so that she has enough money for the telescope?
questions.explanation: She needs $1{,}500 - 420 = 1{,}080$ more dollars, and $1{,}080 \div 90 = 12$ weeks. The choice 17 ignores the money she has already saved.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A potter needs 2 hours to make a small vase and 5 hours to make a large vase, and she has at most 60 hours to work this week. She wants to make at least twice as many small vases as large vases. What is the greatest number of large vases she can make this week?
questions.explanation: Let $s$ and $L$ be the numbers of small and large vases. Since $s \ge 2L$, the time is at least $2(2L) + 5L = 9L$, so $9L \le 60$ and $L \le \dfrac{20}{3}$. The greatest whole number is 6 (12 small and 6 large vases take 54 hours); 7 large vases would need at least 63 hours.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A small farm bridge has a weight limit of 4,000 kilograms. A tractor that weighs 2,650 kilograms will cross the bridge pulling an empty trailer that weighs 400 kilograms, and the trailer will be loaded with sacks of grain that weigh 50 kilograms each. What is the greatest number of sacks the trailer can carry across the bridge without exceeding the weight limit?
questions.explanation: The total weight must satisfy $2{,}650 + 400 + 50s \le 4{,}000$, so $50s \le 950$ and $s \le 19$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Noah has \$60 to spend on notebooks that cost \$4.50 each. Which inequality represents the possible numbers of notebooks, $n$, that Noah can buy?
questions.explanation: $n$ notebooks cost $4.50n$ dollars, and that total can be at most 60 dollars.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Caterer A charges \$350 plus \$18 per guest. Caterer B charges \$200 plus \$24 per guest. What is the least number of guests for which Caterer A charges less than Caterer B?
questions.explanation: Caterer A is cheaper when $350 + 18g < 200 + 24g$, which gives $150 < 6g$, or $g > 25$. The least whole number greater than 25 is 26. At exactly 25 guests, both caterers charge \$800.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A phone plan costs \$12 per month and includes 200 text messages. Each text message beyond the first 200 costs \$0.05. Ethan wants his monthly bill to be at most \$20. What is the greatest total number of text messages he can send in a month?
questions.explanation: Only texts beyond 200 cost extra: $12 + 0.05(t - 200) \le 20$, so $t - 200 \le 160$ and $t \le 360$. 160 is only the number of extra texts.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $n$ is a solution to the inequality $15 - 4n > 3$?
questions.explanation: Subtract 15: $-4n > -12$. Dividing by $-4$ reverses the inequality: $n < 3$. Only 2 is less than 3; $n = 3$ makes the two sides equal.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A farmer has at most 120 hectares of land and at most 4,800 hours of labor for the season. Each hectare of wheat needs 30 hours of labor, and each hectare of cotton needs 60 hours. If the farmer plants $w$ hectares of wheat and $c$ hectares of cotton, which system of inequalities represents these conditions?
questions.explanation: \"At most\" means $\le$. The land used is $w + c$, and the labor used is $30w + 60c$, since wheat takes 30 hours per hectare and cotton takes 60.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: An elevator in an office building can carry at most 900 kilograms. A worker who weighs 75 kilograms is moving boxes that weigh 24 kilograms each and must ride in the elevator with them. What is the greatest number of boxes the worker can take in one trip?
questions.explanation: $75 + 24b \le 900$ gives $24b \le 825$, so $b \le 34.375$. The number of boxes must be a whole number that does not exceed this, so the greatest is 34. Rounding up to 35 would overload the elevator, and ignoring the worker gives 37.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $x$ is NOT a solution to the inequality $5 - 2x \le 1$?
questions.explanation: Subtract 5: $-2x \le -4$. Dividing by $-2$ reverses the inequality: $x \ge 2$. Only 1 is less than 2.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A bakery uses 0.5 kilogram of flour for each loaf of bread and 0.8 kilogram of flour for each cake. On a given day, it has at most 40 kilograms of flour and must make at least 30 loaves and at least 10 cakes. Which combination of $x$ loaves and $y$ cakes satisfies all of these conditions?
questions.explanation: Check $0.5x + 0.8y \le 40$, $x \ge 30$, and $y \ge 10$. For $x = 30$, $y = 30$: $15 + 24 = 39 \le 40$, and both minimums are met. The second choice needs 40.8 kilograms of flour, the third has too few loaves, and the fourth has too few cakes.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A delivery robot can carry at most 25 kilograms. It always carries a 4-kilogram tool kit, plus $b$ boxes that weigh 1.5 kilograms each. Which inequality represents the possible numbers of boxes the robot can carry?
questions.explanation: The total weight is the tool kit plus the boxes, $4 + 1.5b$, and "at most 25" means $\le 25$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Grace has \$60 to spend on art supplies. She has already spent \$12 on paints, and sketchbooks cost \$8 each. What is the greatest number of sketchbooks she can buy?
questions.explanation: She needs $12 + 8s \le 60$, so $8s \le 48$ and $s \le 6$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A robotics team can spend at most \$600 on motors, which cost \$45 each, and sensors, which cost \$20 each. The team must buy at least 4 motors and at least 6 sensors. What is the greatest number of sensors the team can buy?
questions.explanation: To leave the most money for sensors, buy the minimum 4 motors: $600 - 4(45) = 420$, and $420 \div 20 = 21$ sensors. 30 ignores the required motors.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A freight elevator can safely carry at most 1,200 kilograms. An operator who weighs 80 kilograms rides with boxes that weigh 35 kilograms each. What is the greatest number of boxes the elevator can safely carry on one trip with the operator?
questions.explanation: $80 + 35b \le 1{,}200$ gives $35b \le 1{,}120$, so $b \le 32$. *34* ignores the operator's weight.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Isla has \$150 to spend on school supplies. She buys one set of pens for \$15 and some notebooks that cost \$9 each. What is the greatest number of notebooks she can buy?
questions.explanation: $15 + 9n \le 150$ gives $9n \le 135$, so $n \le 15$. *16* forgets the cost of the pens.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A bakery makes cakes and pies. Each cake requires 0.75 hour of oven time, and each pie requires 0.5 hour. This week the oven is available for at most 30 hours, and the bakery must make at least 12 cakes. What is the greatest number of pies the bakery can make this week?
questions.explanation: To make the most pies, make the fewest cakes: 12 cakes use $12 \times 0.75 = 9$ hours. Then $9 + 0.5p \le 30$ gives $p \le 42$. *60* ignores the required cakes.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A delivery van can carry at most 1,200 kilograms. The driver weighs 80 kilograms, and each box of apples weighs 35 kilograms. What is the greatest number of boxes the van can carry along with the driver?

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following is the solution to the inequality $-2x + 7 \le 1$?
questions.explanation: Subtract 7: $-2x \le -6$. Dividing by $-2$ reverses the inequality: $x \ge 3$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Oscar has at most \$30 to spend on notebooks, which cost \$3 each, and pens, which cost \$1.50 each. He wants to buy at least 14 items in total. What is the greatest number of notebooks he can buy?
questions.explanation: With $n$ notebooks and $p$ pens, $3n + 1.5p \le 30$ and $n + p \ge 14$. Using the fewest pens, $p = 14 - n$, gives $3n + 1.5(14 - n) \le 30$, so $1.5n \le 9$ and $n \le 6$. Six notebooks and 8 pens cost exactly \$30.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A delivery van has a load limit of 1,200 kilograms: the total weight of the driver and the boxes in the van cannot exceed this limit. The driver weighs 80 kilograms, and each box weighs 35 kilograms. What is the greatest number of boxes the van can carry?
questions.explanation: $80 + 35b \le 1{,}200$ gives $35b \le 1{,}120$, so $b \le 32$. Forgetting the driver gives $1{,}200 \div 35 \approx 34.3$, which leads to 34.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which inequality represents the statement "a number $n$ increased by 7 is at least 15"?
questions.explanation: "Increased by 7" is $n + 7$, and "at least 15" means greater than or equal to 15: $n + 7 \ge 15$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A bakery sells round loaves for \$8 each and flatbreads for \$3 each. On a certain day, the bakery sells exactly 120 items and needs its total sales to be at least \$600. What is the minimum number of round loaves the bakery must sell that day?
questions.explanation: With $r$ round loaves, it sells $120 - r$ flatbreads: $8r + 3(120 - r) \ge 600$. So $5r + 360 \ge 600$, $r \ge 48$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A river ferry can carry at most 2,400 kilograms of cargo. A truck weighing 1,450 kilograms is already on board. What is the greatest number of 45-kilogram sacks of flour that can also be loaded onto the ferry?
questions.explanation: $1{,}450 + 45s \le 2{,}400$ gives $45s \le 950$, so $s \le \dfrac{950}{45} \approx 21.1$. The greatest whole number of sacks is 21; 22 sacks would go over the limit.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A phone plan costs \$12 per month plus \$0.05 for each text message sent. A customer wants to spend at most \$20 this month. What is the greatest number of text messages the customer can send?

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A bakery makes small cakes that sell for \$6 each and large cakes that sell for \$15 each. Each day it can make at most 40 cakes in total, and it needs to earn at least \$456 from cake sales. If every cake it makes is sold, what is the greatest number of small cakes the bakery can make in one day and still meet its goal?
questions.explanation: With $s$ small and $\ell$ large cakes, $s + \ell \le 40$ and $6s + 15\ell \ge 456$. To allow the most small cakes, make all the others large: $\ell = 40 - s$. Then $6s + 15(40 - s) \ge 456$, so $600 - 9s \ge 456$ and $s \le 16$. Check: 16 small and 24 large cakes earn $6(16) + 15(24) = 456$ dollars.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: If $3 \le 2x - 5 \le 11$, what is the greatest possible value of $4x - 1$?
questions.explanation: Add 5 to each part: $8 \le 2x \le 16$, so $4 \le x \le 8$. The greatest value of $4x - 1$ is $4(8) - 1 = 31$. (8 is the greatest value of $x$, not of $4x - 1$.)

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $x$ satisfies the inequality $3x - 4 > 2x + 6$?
questions.explanation: Subtract $2x$ and add 4: $x > 10$. Only 11 is greater than 10; 10 itself does not satisfy a strict inequality.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following points $(x, y)$ satisfies the inequality $y > 2x - 1$?
questions.explanation: Test each point. For $(0, 0)$: $0 > 2(0) - 1 = -1$ is true. For the others, $2 > 3$, $0 > 1$ and $4 > 5$ are all false.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A school can spend at most \$600 on calculators and rulers. Calculators cost \$18 each and rulers cost \$2 each. If the school buys 25 calculators, what is the greatest number of rulers it can buy?
questions.explanation: The calculators cost $25 \times 18 = 450$ dollars, leaving $600 - 450 = 150$ dollars. At \$2 each, that buys $150 \div 2 = 75$ rulers.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which inequality describes all solutions of $-2x + 5 \le 11$?
questions.explanation: Subtract 5: $-2x \le 6$. Dividing by $-2$ reverses the inequality: $x \ge -3$. Choice A forgets to reverse it.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A phone plan costs \$20 per month plus \$0.10 for each text message sent. Mia wants to spend no more than \$35 this month. What is the greatest number of text messages she can send?

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: $$y > 2x + 1$$ $$y < -x + 7$$ Which of the following points $(x, y)$ is a solution to the system of inequalities?
questions.explanation: For $(1, 4)$: $4 > 3$ and $4 < 6$, so both are true. $(2, 5)$ fails the first inequality because $5 > 5$ is false, $(0, 8)$ fails the second, and $(3, 3)$ fails the first.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Adult tickets to a play cost \$8 and child tickets cost \$5. A group can spend at most \$100 on tickets. Which inequality represents the possible numbers of adult tickets $a$ and child tickets $c$ the group can buy?
questions.explanation: The cost is $8a + 5c$, and "at most \$100" means it is less than or equal to 100.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which inequality describes all solutions of $x + 7 < 12$?
questions.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides: $x < 5$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: How many integers $x$ satisfy $3 < 2x - 1 \le 11$?
questions.explanation: Add 1: $4 < 2x \le 12$. Divide by 2: $2 < x \le 6$. The integers are 3, 4, 5 and 6, so there are 4.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $x$ is NOT a solution to the inequality $5 - x \ge 2$?
questions.explanation: Solve: $-x \ge -3$, so $x \le 3$. The value 4 is greater than 3, so it is not a solution. The value 3 is a solution because the inequality includes "equal to."

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which inequality describes all solutions of $4x \ge 20$?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 4, a positive number, so the inequality sign stays the same: $x \ge 5$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A theater has 400 seats. Each ticket costs either \$12 or \$20. For one show, all 400 seats are sold, and the theater must earn at least \$6,000. What is the least number of \$20 tickets that must be sold?

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: What is the least integer value of $x$ that satisfies $3(x - 2) > 9$?
questions.explanation: Divide by 3: $x - 2 > 3$, so $x > 5$. The least integer greater than 5 is 6.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which inequality describes all solutions of $x - 4 > 6$?
questions.explanation: Add 4 to both sides: $x > 10$. The inequality is strict, so 10 itself is not included.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A truck can carry at most 2,000 kilograms. It is already carrying one crate that weighs 350 kilograms. What is the greatest number of 25-kilogram boxes the truck can also carry?
questions.explanation: The remaining capacity is $2{,}000 - 350 = 1{,}650$ kilograms, and $1{,}650 \div 25 = 66$ boxes. Choice A ignores the crate.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies the inequality $5x - 7 < 28$?
questions.explanation: Add 7: $5x < 35$, so $x < 7$. The greatest integer less than 7 is $6$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Dominique has spent \$118 on office supplies for her business this month. She does not want her total monthly expenses on office supplies to exceed her budget of \$274. What is the maximum amount of additional money Dominique can spend on office supplies this month?
questions.explanation: She can spend at most $274 - 118 = 156$ more dollars. Choice D adds the amounts instead of subtracting.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Rebecca is collecting 60-milliliter samples of river water and 10-milliliter samples of lake water. She needs to collect a total of at least 960 milliliters of river water and lake water, where the number of samples of lake water is twice the number of samples of river water. Which inequality represents this situation, where $x$ is the number of samples of river water that Rebecca needs to collect?
questions.explanation: There are $x$ river samples of 60 mL and $2x$ lake samples of 10 mL, for $60x + 10(2x)$ mL in total. "At least 960" means $\geq 960$. Choices A and B put the $2x$ on the river samples.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Pilar has spent \$125 on office supplies for her business this month. She does not want her total monthly expenses on office supplies to exceed her budget of \$244. What is the maximum additional amount, in dollars, that Pilar can spend on office supplies this month?
questions.explanation: $125 + x \le 244$ gives $x \le 119$, so she can spend at most \$119 more.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A student is hanging $x$ cubes that weigh 2.7 pounds each and $y$ spheres that weigh 3.4 pounds each from a frame. The combined total weight of the cubes and spheres must exceed 19 pounds. Which inequality represents this situation?
questions.explanation: The cubes weigh $2.7x$ and the spheres $3.4y$ pounds. "Exceed" means greater than: $2.7x + 3.4y > 19$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Rebecca is collecting 50-milliliter samples of river water and 10-milliliter samples of lake water. She needs to collect at least 910 milliliters of water in total, and the number of lake water samples is twice the number of river water samples, $x$. Which inequality represents this situation?
questions.explanation: There are $x$ river samples (50 mL each) and $2x$ lake samples (10 mL each), for $50x + 10(2x)$ mL in all. "At least 910" means $\ge 910$. A and B put the $2x$ on the wrong sample type.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt:
$x + 4y > 3$

Which of the following describes the graph of the solutions to the given inequality in the $xy$-plane?
choices: A dashed line through $(3, 0)$ and $(0, 0.75)$, with the region above the line shaded
A dashed line through $(3, 0)$ and $(0, 0.75)$, with the region below the line shaded
A dashed line through $(0.75, 0)$ and $(0, 3)$, with the region to the right of the line shaded
A dashed line through $(0.75, 0)$ and $(0, 3)$, with the region to the left of the line shaded
questions.explanation: The boundary $x + 4y = 3$ has intercepts $(3, 0)$ and $(0, 0.75)$, and it is dashed because $>$ excludes the line. Solving for $y$ gives $y > \frac{3 - x}{4}$, so the region above the line is shaded. (Test $(0, 0)$: $0 > 3$ is false, so the origin, below the line, is not shaded.)

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: The shaded region shown represents the solutions to which inequality?
questions.explanation: The dashed line passes through $(0, 1)$ and $(1, 5)$, so it is $y = 4x + 1$. The shading is below and to the right of the line, so $y < 4x + 1$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A delivery van can carry at most $1{,}500$ pounds. The driver weighs $180$ pounds, and each box weighs $40$ pounds. Which inequality represents the number of boxes, $b$, the van can carry along with the driver?
questions.explanation: Total weight is $40b + 180$, and it can be at most $1{,}500$: $40b + 180 \le 1{,}500$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A number $x$ is at most $27$ less than $3$ times the value of $y$. If the value of $y$ is $8$, what is the greatest possible value of $x$?
questions.explanation: "At most $27$ less than $3$ times $y$" means $x \le 3y - 27$. With $y = 8$: $x \le 24 - 27 = -3$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: The shaded region shown represents the solutions to which inequality?
questions.explanation: The dashed line passes through $(0, 5)$ and $(1, 8)$, so it is $y = 3x + 5$. The shading is below and to the right of it: $y < 3x + 5$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt:
$y \le x + 8$
$y \ge -3x - 8$

Which point $(x, y)$ is a solution to the given system of inequalities in the $xy$-plane?
questions.explanation: Check $(5, 0)$: $0 \le 13$ and $0 \ge -23$, both true. $(0, -9)$ fails the second ($-9 \ge -8$ is false), $(0, 9)$ fails the first, and $(-5, 0)$ fails the second ($0 \ge 7$ is false).

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which inequality has the solutions represented by the shaded region in the graph shown?
questions.explanation: The dashed line passes through $(-4, 0)$ and $(0, 12)$, so its slope is $\frac{12}{4} = 3$ and it is $y = 3x + 12$. The shading is below and to the right of the line: $y < 3x + 12$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A biologist recorded the pinching force of wild coconut crabs. The lowest pinching force recorded was $86.2$ newtons and the highest pinching force recorded was $121.4$ newtons. Which inequality is true for all values of $c$, where $c$ represents any pinching force, in newtons, recorded for these wild coconut crabs?
questions.explanation: Every recorded force is at least the lowest value and at most the highest: $86.2 \le c \le 121.4$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which shaded region represents the solutions to the inequality $y \le -\frac{1}{4}x + 7$?
questions.explanation: The boundary line has a negative slope ($-\frac{1}{4}$) and $y$-intercept $7$, so it falls from left to right; that rules out A and B. "$y \le$" means the region below the line is shaded, which is Graph C.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: To earn a bachelor's degree at a certain university, students are required to complete at least $120$ credit hours. If a student has completed $42$ credit hours, what is the minimum number of additional credit hours the student is required to complete to earn a bachelor's degree at this university?
questions.explanation: $120 - 42 = 78$ more credit hours.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which shaded region represents the solutions to the inequality $4x + 5y < 9$?
questions.explanation: Solve for $y$: $y < -\frac{4}{5}x + \frac{9}{5}$. The line has a negative slope, ruling out A and B, and the region below it is shaded (the origin works: $0 < 9$). That is Graph C. (The PDF key said D, but D shades the region above the line.)

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A school club is selling candles for \$12 each and soap bars for \$5 each. The club needs to earn at least \$600, and it has no more than $80$ items to sell. Which point $(c, s)$, where $c$ is the number of candles and $s$ is the number of soap bars sold, satisfies both conditions?

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: At the beginning of the year, Imani has \$170 in her account. Each month this year, she will deposit between \$30 and \$60 into the account. Which inequality represents all possibilities for the total amount of money $x$, in dollars, in Imani's account after $10$ months of deposits this year?
questions.explanation: Ten deposits add between $10(30) = 300$ and $10(60) = 600$ dollars to the \$170, so $470 \le x \le 770$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Sam has \$50 to spend on movie tickets that cost \$6 each. Which inequality represents the possible numbers of tickets, $t$, that Sam can buy?
questions.explanation: $t$ tickets cost $6t$ dollars, which can be at most \$50: $6t \le 50$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A delivery truck can carry at most $2{,}000$ pounds of cargo. It carries boxes that weigh $45$ pounds each and crates that weigh $80$ pounds each. If the truck is carrying $20$ crates, what is the greatest number of boxes it can also carry?
questions.explanation: The crates weigh $20(80) = 1{,}600$ pounds, leaving $400$ pounds. $45b \le 400$ gives $b \le 8.9$, so at most $8$ boxes.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $x$ satisfies the inequality $2x + 7 > 19$?
questions.explanation: $2x > 12$, so $x > 6$. Only $8$ is greater than $6$; $x = 6$ gives $19 > 19$, which is false.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt:
$y \le x + 14$
$y \ge -3x - 14$

Which point $(x, y)$ is a solution to the given system of inequalities in the $xy$-plane?
questions.explanation: Check $(8, 0)$: $0 \le 22$ and $0 \ge -38$, both true. $(0, -15)$ fails the second inequality, $(0, 15)$ fails the first, and $(-8, 0)$ fails the second ($0 \ge 10$ is false).
